name: iwl_dbgfs_send_hcmd_write
prose: Writes a hex-encoded host command to the firmware. Returns -EIO if iwl_trans_fw_running(fwrt->trans) is false; -EINVAL if count < header_size+1 (21) or count > 4096; -ENOMEM if kmalloc of (count-1)/2 bytes fails; the hex2bin error (non-zero) if the input is not valid hex; -EINVAL (with an IWL_ERR message) if count != header_size + 2*length + 1 where length is the decoded be16 length field; -EPERM if fwrt->ops or ops->send_hcmd is NULL. Otherwise it calls ops->send_hcmd and, if that returns a negative value, returns it. If it returns >= 0 and hcmd.flags has CMD_WANT_SKB it calls iwl_free_resp (so the response buffer is freed only on that non-negative path, not when send_hcmd fails); the final return is the callback value if non-zero (positive values included) or count when it returned 0. The temporary buffer is kfree'd on every path after the kmalloc succeeded (the out label); the earlier returns happen before it exists.
note: Slice started at 252 in the middle; real head at debugfs.c:240. Reviewer (round 15) right: iwl_free_resp skipped at line 283-284 when send_hcmd returns <0 (old prose said freed always for CMD_WANT_SKB).

name: iwl_parse_tlv_firmware
prose: Parses a TLV-format firmware image (static int iwl_parse_tlv_firmware, iwl-drv.c:809; the slice began in the middle of the TLV switch). Returns -EINVAL if len < sizeof(*ucode) (830) or the magic is not IWL_TLV_UCODE_MAGIC (836); it then records ucode_ver, human_readable and fw_version in drv->fw and walks TLVs while len >= sizeof(*tlv). A TLV with length greater than the remaining len returns -EINVAL (873). Per-type handlers jump to invalid_tlv_len/tlv_error (both end in -EINVAL after logging and optionally a hex dump) for a wrong fixed size or an invalid value: e.g. a wrong-size probe/flags/capa/evtlog/phy/cpu-count/scan-channel/fw-version/num-stations/num-links/umac-lmac-debug/paging TLV, a bad default-calibration entry (iwl_set_default_calib), num stations > IWL_STATION_COUNT_MAX or links > IWL_FW_MAX_LINK_ID+1. Other direct -EINVAL returns: NUM_OF_CPU outside 1..2 (1082), paging size > MAX_PAGING_IMAGE_SIZE (1247) or not a multiple of FW_PAGING_SIZE (1254), a second CMD_VERSIONS TLV when capa->cmd_versions is already set (1405). A wrong-size FW_DBG_DUMP_LST TLV is only logged and skipped (1219-1222), not an error; a bad/duplicate debug dest, conf or trigger TLV is also logged and skipped; unknown TLV types are ignored. A CMD_VERSIONS length that is not a multiple of the entry size is truncated down, not rejected. Returns -ENOMEM when krealloc of dbg_mem_tlv (1280), kmemdup of iml (1290), cmd_versions, phy_integration_ver, pc_data or kvmemdup of pnvm_data fails. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if the usniffer capability is not unified, a usniffer config was requested and *usniffer_images is zero (1456-1460), and -EINVAL if bytes remain in len (1463-1473); otherwise 0. Fields in drv->fw, drv->trans->dbg, capa and pieces may already have been set when an error is returned, and heap copies made earlier stay referenced from those structures; this function does not free them. Callee bodies (iwl_store_ucode_sec, iwl_set_default_calib) not read.
note: Slice cut the head (real function starts at iwl-drv.c:809, ends ~1485). Partly read: handlers for INST/DATA/INIT/WOWLAN sections, FLAGS, API/CAPA, DBG_CONF/TRIGGER (1158-1217), RECOVERY_INFO, FSEQ_VERSION, UMAC/LMAC_DEBUG_ADDRS bodies skimmed for return/goto only. Reviewer (round 17) right: wrong-size DUMP_LST is skipped at 1219-1222.

name: iwl_mld_release_frames_from_notif
prose: Static helper (agg.c:45). If baid equals IWL_RX_REORDER_DATA_INVALID_BAID or baid >= ARRAY_SIZE(mld->fw_id_to_ba) it does WARN_ON_ONCE and returns before taking any lock (57-59). Otherwise it calls rcu_read_lock (61), reads mld->fw_id_to_ba[baid] and, if NULL, logs and jumps to out_unlock. It computes sta_id = ffs(ba_data->sta_mask) - 1 (70, no check that sta_mask is non-zero, so a zero mask gives an out-of-range index into fw_id_to_link_sta), looks up the link_sta and if it is an error pointer/NULL or has no ->sta it WARN_ON_ONCEs and goes to out_unlock. Otherwise it calls iwl_mld_reorder_release_frames(mld, link_sta->sta, napi, ba_data, &ba_data->reorder_buf[queue], nssn) (77); what that callee does with head_sn was not read. rcu_read_unlock is executed at out_unlock on every path after the lock was taken. It does not require the caller to be outside an RCU read section: rcu_read_lock nests and its caller iwl_mld_handle_bar_frame_release_notif already holds it (128).
note: Reviewers: original-rejection (precondition wrong) partly right, round 2 right (sta_mask zero not checked, line 70), round 15 right (caller holds rcu_read_lock at agg.c:128). Callee iwl_mld_reorder_release_frames not read.

name: iwl_mld_wowlan_resume
prose: Resume flow after WoWLAN (d3.c:1958). Asserts the wiphy lock (lockdep_assert_wiphy). It reaches the err label (sets mld->fw_status.in_hw_restart = true, ret = 1) if fw_status.in_d3 is false (1976), iwl_mld_get_bss_vif returns NULL (WARN_ON, 1987), the link_conf for the vif's first active link (or link 0) is NULL (WARN_ON, 1997), or iwl_mld_wait_d3_notif returns non-zero (2010; the error is logged, then ret is overwritten with 1). Before the in_d3 check passes nothing is changed; after it passes, resuming is set true and in_d3 cleared. If the zeroed wowlan_status allocation fails (2002) it returns -ENOMEM directly, so fw_status.resuming stays true and in_d3 is already false. If the D3 end flags contain IWL_D0I3_RESET_REQUIRE it sets in_hw_restart and skips the power/regdomain updates but still goes to process_wakeup_results with ret still 0. Otherwise it updates regdomain, MAC power, beacon filter, device power and, if mld->netdetect, calls iwl_mld_scan_stop whose result becomes ret and is returned unchanged at the end (the flow continues even if it is non-zero). In process_wakeup_results: with netdetect it processes the netdetect results and sets mld->netdetect = false (no EMLSR unblock or disconnect there); without netdetect it calls iwl_mld_process_wowlan_status and then iwl_mld_unblock_emlsr(IWL_MLD_EMLSR_BLOCKED_WOWLAN) if that returned true, else ieee80211_resume_disconnect. Both the normal and err paths reach out, which clears fw_status.resuming and frees wowlan_status->wake_packet and wowlan_status when wowlan_status was allocated. Returns 0 on the normal paths (including the RESET_REQUIRE one), 1 on err, -ENOMEM on the allocation failure, or the scan_stop result in the netdetect case.
note: Reviewers: original (ENOMEM leaves resuming set; returns 1 also for !in_d3/WARN) right; round 15 (netdetect success does not unblock EMLSR/disconnect) right. Callees not read.

name: iwl_mld_remove_key
prose: Removes a key from the firmware (key.c:181). Asserts the wiphy lock. It first computes sta_mask and key_flags with iwl_mld_get_key_sta_mask and iwl_mld_get_key_flags. If sta_mask is 0 it returns with nothing else done (191). If key->keyidx is 4 or 5 (IGTK/BIGTK) it uses link_id = key->link_id when that is >= 0, else 0; if iwl_mld_link_dereference_check gives NULL it does WARN_ON and returns without sending the command and without touching hw_key_idx (203-204); otherwise it sets mld_link->igtk = NULL only if it equals key and then decrements mld->num_igtks (the decrement is not conditional on the pointer match). It then calls iwl_mld_remove_key_from_fw, which itself returns without sending anything when CONFIG_PM_SLEEP is set and mld->fw_status.resuming is true (171-172), or when sta_mask is 0 (175); otherwise it sends the SEC_KEY_CMD remove command and ignores its result. Finally it sets key->hw_key_idx = STA_KEY_IDX_INVALID. Returns void.
note: Reviewers: original (early return on link lookup failure; igtk cleared only if matches) right; round 15 (firmware remove skipped while fw_status.resuming) right, key.c:171-172.

name: iwl_mld_handle_missed_beacon_notif
prose: Handles a firmware missed-beacons notification (link.c:526). It maps notif->link_id to a link_conf; if NULL it does WARN_ON and returns (544). It takes vif from link_conf, logs missed counts with IWL_DEBUG_INFO, and if vif is NULL does WARN_ON and returns (555; the debug log has already run). It then records the IWL_FW_INI_TIME_POINT_MISSED_BEACONS time point. If missed_bcon >= IWL_MLD_MISSED_BEACONS_THRESHOLD_LONG: it calls ieee80211_connection_loss(vif) and returns when missed_bcon_since_rx >= IWL_MLD_MISSED_BEACONS_SINCE_RX_THOLD, else logs a warning and returns (561-569). Otherwise, if missed_bcon_since_rx > IWL_MLD_MISSED_BEACONS_THRESHOLD it calls ieee80211_cqm_beacon_loss_notify(vif, GFP_ATOMIC) and, only if iwl_mld_emlsr_active(vif) is false, iwl_mld_int_mlo_scan; execution then continues. It returns without EMLSR exit if hweight16(vif->active_links) <= 1, if notif->other_link_id equals FW_CTXT_ID_INVALID, or if the other link does not resolve (IWL_FW_CHECK). Otherwise it calls iwl_mld_exit_emlsr(mld, vif, IWL_MLD_EMLSR_EXIT_MISSED_BEACON, iwl_mld_get_primary_link(vif)) only when one of the three beacon-loss conditions at lines 613-618 is true. It takes no lock and acquires no reference in this function itself (callees not read). Returns void.
note: Reviewer round 15 right (debug log before the vif WARN_ON, link.c:551-555); original reviewer right (EMLSR exit needs >1 active links and valid other link, scan only if EMLSR inactive).

name: iwl_mld_low_latency_update_counters
prose: Counts VO/VI frames per rx queue for low-latency detection (low_latency.c:260). It dereferences sta (mld_sta->vif, and the vif's fw_id) before any check, so sta and its vif must be valid. It returns with no counter change if mld->low_latency.pkts_counters is NULL (WARN_ON_ONCE, 272), if fw_id >= ARRAY_SIZE(counters->vo_vi) or queue >= mld->trans->info.num_rxqs (WARN_ON_ONCE, 275; ARRAY_SIZE is a compile-time size, it does not read the uninitialised counters pointer), if mld->low_latency.stopped is set (279), or if iwl_mld_is_vo_vi_pkt(hdr) is false (282). Otherwise it increments pkts_counters[queue].vo_vi[fw_id] under spin_lock_bh(&counters->lock), then, outside that lock, sets window_start[fw_id] to jiffies (or 1 when jiffies is 0) if it is zero, and, if time_is_before_jiffies(timestamp + MLD_LL_PERIOD), queues mld->low_latency.work with delay 0 via wiphy_delayed_work_queue. Returns void.
note: Reviewer original right-ish (checks are done in the function); round 15 WRONG: ARRAY_SIZE(counters->vo_vi) at low_latency.c:275 is sizeof-based and does not dereference counters, which is assigned only at 285 (the old prose was fine on that point).

name: iwl_mld_handle_nan_dw_end_notif
prose: Handles the NAN discovery-window-end notification (nan.c:252; the slice cut the head). It logs the band, then returns early with IWL_FW_CHECK failure reporting if mld->nan_device_vif is NULL (so mld_vif is NULL, 262) or if ieee80211_vif_nan_started on it is false (265); it also returns early (WARN_ON) if mld_vif->aux_sta.sta_id == IWL_INVALID_STA (268). Otherwise it flushes the aux station's TX queues with iwl_mld_flush_link_sta_txqs(mld, sta_id) (274). It then selects chan = ieee80211_get_channel(wiphy, 2437) for IWL_NAN_BAND_2GHZ or 5745 for IWL_NAN_BAND_5GHZ; for any other band it reports through IWL_FW_CHECK and returns (after the flush has already been done, so the flush is not skipped for an invalid band). For the two valid bands it calls cfg80211_next_nan_dw_notif(wdev from ieee80211_vif_to_wdev(nan_device_vif), chan, GFP_KERNEL); chan may be NULL if ieee80211_get_channel finds no such channel (not checked). Returns void; no lock is taken here.
note: Previous round dropped it as not a function; it is a real function. Old prose wrongly said no flush on an invalid band (nan.c:274 precedes the switch at 279-292).

name: iwl_mld_he_mac80211_mcs_to_fw_mcs
prose: Static pure helper (tlc.c:200) converting an HE MCS support code to a firmware MCS bitmask. For mcs equal to IEEE80211_HE_MCS_SUPPORT_0_7 it returns BIT(IWL_TLC_MNG_HT_RATE_MCS7 + 1) - 1 = 0xFF (255), for IEEE80211_HE_MCS_SUPPORT_0_9 it returns BIT(MCS9 + 1) - 1 = 0x3FF (1023), for IEEE80211_HE_MCS_SUPPORT_0_11 it returns BIT(MCS11 + 1) - 1 = 0xFFF (4095), and for IEEE80211_HE_MCS_NOT_SUPPORTED it returns 0. For any other value it executes WARN(1, ...) and returns 0. It reads no global state, takes no lock and allocates nothing.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (mcs == 0 ==> result == 255) && (mcs == 1 ==> result == 1023) && (mcs == 2 ==> result == 4095) && (mcs >= 3 ==> result == 0); */
note: Reviewers round 1 and 2 claims (16383, 511) are wrong; round 15 (WARN side effect not in contract) is right about the WARN but the contract only constrains result. Enum values at fw/api/rs.h:106-117 (MCS7=7, MCS9=9, MCS11=11).

name: iwl_mvm_ftm_range_resp
prose: Handler for the firmware FTM range-response notification (ftm-initiator.c:1262; the name iwl_mvm_ftm_range_resp_notif in the packet does not exist, the slice cut the head). It takes (mvm, rxb), asserts mvm->mutex is held, and returns void. It returns with no further effect if mvm->ftm_initiator.req is NULL, if iwl_mvm_ftm_resp_size_validation(notif_ver, pkt_len) fails, or if iwl_mvm_ftm_range_resp_valid(...) returns true for the request_id/num_of_aps of the v8 layout (when FTM_NEW_RANGE_REQ API is present) or of the v5 layout (otherwise); that helper returns true on a bad response. Otherwise it loops over i < num_of_aps and i < IWL_TOF_MAX_APS: it picks fw_ap from the v8, v7, v6 or v5 layout; in the new-API, notif_ver >= 8 case it calls iwl_mvm_ftm_pasn_update_pn(mvm, fw_ap) before looking the peer up, so this call also happens for an entry whose bssid is later found unknown. If iwl_mvm_ftm_find_peer finds no peer for fw_ap->bssid it logs IWL_WARN and continues with the next entry. For a known peer it builds a cfg80211_pmsr_result (status and failure reason from measure_status, busy_retry_time from refusal_period for REQUEST_REJECTED, addr, host_time, type FTM, burst_index = the peer's responses[] count, which it then increments, RSSI/RTT values with valid flags, LCI/civic via iwl_mvm_ftm_get_lci_civic, then iwl_mvm_ftm_rtt_smoothing) and passes it to cfg80211_pmsr_report with GFP_KERNEL. After the loop, if last_in_batch (v8 last_report or v5 last_in_batch) is set it calls cfg80211_pmsr_complete and iwl_mvm_ftm_reset. It allocates no memory that it keeps itself (callee iwl_mvm_ftm_get_lci_civic not read).
note: Slice cut the head; real function starts at ftm-initiator.c:1262 and ends 1406. Old prose said peers are matched but also claimed PASN update was done on the matched entry; it is done before the peer lookup (1316-1318 region, line 52 of function listing).

name: iwl_run_init_mvm_ucode
prose: Runs the INIT firmware and calibrations (fw.c:702). If iwl_mvm_has_unified_ucode(mvm) it returns iwl_run_unified_mvm_ucode(mvm) immediately (711), before the lockdep_assert_held(&mvm->mutex) at 714. Otherwise it asserts mvm->mutex is held, clears rfkill_safe_init_done and registers calib_wait for INIT_COMPLETE_NOTIF/CALIB_RES_NOTIF_PHY_DB. It then, in order: loads the INIT ucode (iwl_mvm_load_ucode_wait_alive), on device family < 8000 sends the BT init config, reads NVM if mvm->nvm_data is NULL, loads the NVM file to the NIC if nvm_file_name is set; each failure sets ret to that callee's value and goes to remove_notif (which removes calib_wait) and then out. If iwl_mvm_is_radio_hw_killed(mvm) is true after the NVM steps it goes to remove_notif with ret still equal to the last successful step's value (0), so it returns 0 without running calibrations. Otherwise it sets rfkill_safe_init_done = true, sends the TX antenna config and PHY config (failures go to remove_notif), then waits for calibration with iwl_wait_notification (timeout MVM_UCODE_CALIB_TIMEOUT): a 0 result goes to out; a non-zero result is reset to 0 if the radio is RF-killed, else it is logged and returned. At out it always sets rfkill_safe_init_done = false, and if mvm->nvm_data is still NULL it kzallocs a small fake NVM (returning -ENOMEM if that fails, overriding ret; otherwise one channel and one bitrate are set up). Returns ret, which is 0, a callee's non-zero result, or -ENOMEM.
note: Reviewer original right (RF-kill path returns 0, line 764-767); round 15 WRONG: load_ucode failure goes to remove_notif then out, where a NULL nvm_data is replaced by the fake NVM (807-821), so nvm_data is non-NULL unless -ENOMEM. The wait helper's own removal of calib_wait on the wait path was not read.

name: iwl_mvm_mac_ampdu_action
prose: mac80211 ampdu_action callback (mac80211.c:1017; the name iwl_mvm_ampdu_action does not exist, the slice cut the head). It reads sta->addr for a debug print (sta is dereferenced before any check) and returns -EACCES without taking mvm->mutex if mvm->nvm_data->sku_cap_11n_enable is false (1032). Otherwise it does mutex_lock(&mvm->mutex) and switches on action. RX_START: if the vif's deflink.ap_sta_id equals the station's deflink.sta_id it sets the TCM mac data's opened_rx_ba_sessions = true and cancel_delayed_work on uapsd_nonagg_detected_wk; this happens before and independent of the next check; then if !iwl_enable_rx_ampdu() ret = -EINVAL, else ret = iwl_mvm_sta_rx_agg(..., *ssn, true, buf_size, timeout). RX_STOP calls iwl_mvm_sta_rx_agg with start false and ssn 0. TX_START returns -EINVAL if !iwl_enable_tx_ampdu(), else iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_start (which gets the ssn pointer). TX_STOP_CONT calls iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_stop; TX_STOP_FLUSH and TX_STOP_FLUSH_CONT call iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_flush; TX_OPERATIONAL calls iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_oper. Any other action does WARN_ON_ONCE and ret = -EINVAL. If ret is 0 it calls iwl_mvm_ampdu_check_trigger with rx_ba_ssn = *ssn for RX_START and 0 otherwise. It then unlocks mvm->mutex on the way out (the early -EACCES return is the only exit before the lock) and returns ret, which is 0 or whatever the dispatched helper or the -EINVAL cases produced.
note: Slice cut the head (real function at mac80211.c:1017-1128). Old prose said the TCM flag/cancel is on success only; it is set before the rx-ampdu-enabled check (1049-1058). Helpers not read.

name: iwl_mvm_pre_channel_switch
prose: Prepares a channel switch (mac80211.c:5473, static). Asserts mvm->mutex is held; clears mvmvif->csa_failed and csa_blocks_tx and fires the FW_DBG_TRIGGER_CHANNEL_SWITCH debug trigger. AP: returns -EBUSY if mvm->csa_vif is set and its bss_conf.csa_active is true (WARN_ONCE), or if mvm->csa_tx_blocked_vif is set; then it assigns mvm->csa_vif = vif, and returns -EBUSY (WARN_ONCE) if mvmvif->csa_countdown is already set, so csa_vif stays assigned in that case; otherwise it sets csa_target_freq and, only when chsw->block_tx and the HW has HANDLES_QUIET_CSA, sets csa_blocks_tx, sets IWL_MVM_TXQ_STATE_STOP_AP_CSA on the vif txq and blocks station txqs via ieee80211_iterate_stations_atomic. STATION: sets csa_blocks_tx = chsw->block_tx; if the firmware knows CHANNEL_SWITCH_ERROR_NOTIF (notif version non-zero) it breaks out of the switch and skips everything else in this case (no delayed work, no CSA command, no csa_count update). Otherwise it returns -EBUSY if the vif is not associated or has no dtim_period, may schedule csa_work (immediately if chsw->delay > IWL_MAX_CSA_BLOCK_TX, or after IWL_MAX_CSA_BLOCK_TX ms if block_tx and the countdown is long or zero), then on firmware without CHANNEL_SWITCH_CMD capability calls iwl_mvm_old_pre_chan_sw_sta and returns its non-zero error, or else calls iwl_mvm_schedule_client_csa and ignores its result; it then records csa_count = chsw->count and csa_misbehave = false. Other interface types do nothing in the switch. After the switch it sets mvmvif->ps_disabled = true, returns the error from iwl_mvm_power_update_ps if non-zero, and otherwise calls iwl_mvm_teardown_tdls_peers and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original right (new FW flow breaks early; client CSA error ignored); round 15 right (csa_count recording also skipped on that path, 5573). iwl_mvm_old_pre_chan_sw_sta and iwl_mvm_schedule_client_csa not read (so the disable_beacon_filter claim of the old prose is not verified here).

name: iwl_mvm_mld_vif_cfg_changed_station
prose: Handles station-mode vif config changes (mld-mac80211.c:601, static, returns void). If changes == BSS_CHANGED_IDLE exactly, it returns at once, before the MAC context push and before mvmvif->associated is updated. Otherwise it calls iwl_mvm_mld_mac_ctxt_changed (logging an error on failure but continuing) and sets mvmvif->associated = vif->cfg.assoc. If changes has BSS_CHANGED_ASSOC: when vif->cfg.assoc is true it clears session_prot_connection_loss, requests statistics and periodic system statistics, calls iwl_mvm_sf_update and iwl_mvm_power_vif_assoc (these two calls appear at 634-635 and again at 668-671), zeroes each valid link's beacon_stats, for p2p vifs sets dynamic SMPS per link, and checks under rcu_read_lock whether a link_conf has dtim_period 0; if so and IWL_MVM_STATUS_IN_HW_RESTART is not set it calls iwl_mvm_protect_assoc(mvm, vif, 0). When vif->cfg.assoc is false and iwl_mvm_mld_vif_have_valid_ap_sta is true it calls iwl_mvm_mei_host_disassociated, turns off periodic system statistics and calls iwl_mvm_sf_update, with a WARN_ONCE if that fails and no HW restart was requested. In both cases iwl_mvm_bss_info_changed_station_assoc(mvm, vif, changes) is then called (687), also when disassociating or when no valid ap_sta exists. If changes has BSS_CHANGED_PS it calls iwl_mvm_smps_workaround and iwl_mvm_power_update_mac, logging an error on failure. Callees not read.
note: Reviewer original right (early return skips mvmvif->associated update, line 614-621); round 15 right (bss_info_changed_station_assoc called for any ASSOC change, line 687 is outside the if/else).

name: iwl_mvm_set_mac80211_rx_flag
prose: Decides from the firmware MPDU status word whether an RX frame is kept and what it reports (rx.c:139, static, returns u32). Returns 0 without touching stats or *crypt_len if the frame is not protected or the cipher field is SEC_NO_ENC (145-148), or if it is SEC_ENC_ERR (151-153). For CCM it returns (u32)-1 if MIC_OK is not set; else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED and *crypt_len = IEEE80211_CCMP_HDR_LEN and returns 0. For TKIP: if the DEPRECATE_TTAK API is absent and TTAK_OK is not set it returns 0 leaving stats and *crypt_len untouched (software decrypts); otherwise (TTAK ok, or the API deprecates the TTAK check so the bit is not consulted) it sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_TKIP_IV_LEN and falls into the WEP case. WEP/TKIP: returns -1 if ICV_OK is not set (for TKIP *crypt_len has already been set); else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED, sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_WEP_IV_LEN only for WEP, and returns 0. EXT_ENC: returns -1 if MIC_OK is not set, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED and returns 0 leaving *crypt_len unchanged. Any other cipher value logs an unhandled-algorithm warning (unless monitor_on) and returns 0 with no flag or length change.
note: Reviewers: original right (TTAK failure -> 0 untouched, only when the API is not deprecated); round 15 right that the deprecated-TTAK path is not untouched (rx.c:167-172, crypt_len set at 171, and DECRYPTED possible after the ICV check).

name: iwl_mvm_rx_crypto
prose: Checks the firmware's crypto status for a received MPDU (rxmq.c:417, static, returns int). It returns -1 first if the PHY info has IWL_RX_MPDU_PHY_AMPDU, the status cipher field is SEC_UNKNOWN and mvm->monitor_on is false (432-437). If the frame is a management frame without the protected bit it returns whatever iwl_mvm_rx_mgmt_prot(sta, hdr, desc, status, stats) returns (callee not read). If the frame is not protected, or the cipher is SEC_NONE, it returns 0 without setting any flag or *crypt_len (443-446); on FreeBSD an SEC_ENC_ERR cipher also returns 0 untouched (451-453). Then by cipher: CCM or GCM returns -1 on !MIC_OK, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED | RX_FLAG_MIC_STRIPPED and *crypt_len = IEEE80211_CCMP_HDR_LEN and returns 0. TKIP returns 0 untouched if the DEPRECATE_TTAK API is absent and TTAK_OK is clear; else (gen2 devices without MIC_OK also get RX_FLAG_MMIC_ERROR) it sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_TKIP_IV_LEN and falls into WEP: returns -1 if ICV_OK is clear, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED, sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_WEP_IV_LEN only for WEP, and, if FH_RSCSR_RADA_EN is set in pkt_flags, also RX_FLAG_ICV_STRIPPED (plus RX_FLAG_MMIC_STRIPPED on gen2) and returns 0. EXT_ENC returns -1 if MIC_OK is clear, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED and returns 0 leaving *crypt_len unchanged. The CMAC/GMAC cipher (break) and any unlisted cipher (default; may log a warning for unicast non-monitor frames) both fall out of the switch and return 0 with no flag change.
note: Reviewers: original right (0 returned without *crypt_len for deferred TKIP, EXT_ENC; mgmt path delegated); round 15 PARTLY WRONG: CMAC/GMAC and default return 0 (rxmq.c:504-524), not -1; it is right that unprotected non-mgmt frames return 0 without DECRYPTED.

name: iwl_mvm_check_running_scans
prose: Decides whether a new scan of the given type can start (scan.c:2628, static). First: if type is IWL_MVM_SCAN_SCHED or IWL_MVM_SCAN_NETDETECT and scan_status has a sched or net-detect scan running, it returns -EBUSY even if scan slots are free (2644-2646). Then, if iwl_mvm_num_scans(mvm) < mvm->max_scans (a slot is free) it returns 0 (2648). Only when no slot is free does it switch on type: REGULAR returns -EBUSY if a regular scan (REGULAR_MASK) is running, else returns the result of iwl_mvm_scan_stop(SCHED, true); SCHED returns -EBUSY if SCHED_MASK is set, else the result of iwl_mvm_scan_stop(REGULAR, true); NETDETECT returns 0 for a non-unified image (no CNSLDTD_D3_D0_IMG capability), and for a unified image returns iwl_mvm_scan_stop of the running regular scan, else of the running sched scan; if neither is running (or for an unknown type) it does WARN_ON(1) and returns -EIO. So the return is 0, -EBUSY, -EIO, or whatever iwl_mvm_scan_stop returns (including an error from it).
note: Reviewers: original right (scan_stop result passed through); round 15 right (-EBUSY for the same type only when no free slot, except sched/netdetect which return -EBUSY earlier regardless of free slots). iwl_mvm_scan_stop and iwl_mvm_num_scans not read.

name: iwl_mvm_sta_rx_agg
prose: Starts or stops an RX block-ack session (sta.c:2893). Asserts mvm->mutex is held. If start and mvm->rx_ba_sessions >= the session limit (IWL_MAX_BAID with the new TX API, else IWL_MAX_BAID_OLD) it returns -ENOSPC. With the new RX API and start it kzallocs baid_data (returns -ENOMEM on failure). The baid passed to the firmware is mvm_sta->tid_to_baid[tid] when stopping with the new RX API, else -1. It calls iwl_mvm_fw_baid_op unless this is a stop during IWL_MVM_STATUS_IN_HW_RESTART (then baid keeps that initial value, which is -1 with the old RX API). If the resulting baid is negative (a firmware/command error from iwl_mvm_fw_baid_op, or the initial -1) it frees baid_data (kfree, NULL-safe) and returns that negative value (so a stop in a HW restart with the old RX API returns -1). On start success it increments mvm->rx_ba_sessions; with the old RX API it returns 0 there; with the new RX API it fills baid_data (baid, timeout, last_rx, timer, sta_mask, buf_size), stores baid in mvm_sta->tid_to_baid[tid], arms the session timer when timeout != 0, initialises the reorder buffer, WARNs if baid_map[baid] is already set and publishes baid_data with rcu_assign_pointer; returns 0. On stop success it first decrements rx_ba_sessions if it is > 0; with the old RX API it returns 0; with the new API it returns -EINVAL (WARN_ON) if tid_to_baid[tid] is IWL_RX_REORDER_DATA_INVALID_BAID or if baid_map[baid] is NULL (rx_ba_sessions has already been decremented and the map entry left as it was in those cases); otherwise it frees the reorder buffer, shuts down the timer, clears baid_map[baid] and kfree_rcu's baid_data, and returns 0. Callees (fw_baid_op and its variants) not read, so their exact error values are not claimed.
note: Reviewers: original right (old API has no baid_map; stop failures decrement before -EINVAL); round 15 partly checked: -1 on restart stop with old API is right (2950-2964); the -EINVAL for a missing BAID_VALID flag is inside iwl_mvm_fw_baid_op_sta/_cmd, not read.

name: iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_stop
prose: Stops a TX aggregation session for one tid (sta.c:3358). If IWL_MVM_STATUS_IN_HW_RESTART is set it calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe and returns 0 right away, without taking the station lock, touching tid_data or asserting the mutex (3370-3373). Otherwise it takes mvmsta->lock (spin_lock_bh), clears the tid bit in mvmsta->agg_tids and calls iwl_mvm_unreserve_agg_queue, which asserts mvm->mutex is held on every call (so the mutex is needed for all paths past the restart check) and on the old TX API frees a RESERVED queue and sets tid_data->txq_id to IWL_MVM_INVALID_QUEUE. Then by tid_data->state: IWL_AGG_ON sets ssn from seq_number, sets ssn to 0xffff and state to IWL_AGG_OFF, drops the lock, calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe and iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg(..., false) and returns 0; IWL_AGG_STARTING or IWL_EMPTYING_HW_QUEUE_ADDBA calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe, sets state to IWL_AGG_OFF, and returns 0 after unlocking; any other state logs errors and returns -EINVAL after unlocking, leaving the state unchanged (the agg_tids bit has already been cleared and unreserve already run in this case).
note: Reviewers: original right (0/-EINVAL returns and state changes missing in the old annotation); round 15 right (iwl_mvm_unreserve_agg_queue asserts the mutex, sta.c:3340, for all non-restart paths).

name: iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_flush
prose: Flushes a TX aggregation session (sta.c:3431). It does not check IN_HW_RESTART. It takes mvmsta->lock, records the old tid state, sets tid_data->state = IWL_AGG_OFF, clears the tid bit in agg_tids and unlocks, then calls iwl_mvm_unreserve_agg_queue (which asserts mvm->mutex is held, so the mutex is a precondition on every call). If the old state was >= IWL_AGG_ON it drains the station (iwl_mvm_drain_sta true), flushes the queue (iwl_mvm_flush_sta_tids and iwl_trans_wait_txq_empty with the new TX API, else iwl_mvm_flush_tx_path and iwl_trans_wait_tx_queues_empty) logging but ignoring a flush error, undrains the station and calls iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg(mvm, sta, tid, txq_id, false). For an older state none of that is done. It returns 0 in every path (no error return exists in this function); it does not call ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe.
note: Reviewers: original right (return is 0, flush/drain side effects); round 15 right (mutex assert in iwl_mvm_unreserve_agg_queue, sta.c:3340). Callees iwl_mvm_drain_sta/flush helpers not read.

name: iwl_mvm_redirect_queue
prose: Moves a TX queue to the FIFO of another AC (sta.c:704, static). Returns -EINVAL (WARN_ON) if the new TX API is in use (715). Returns 0 without any change if ac <= mvm->queue_info[queue].mac80211_ac and force is false (726; since AC numbering is flipped, it redirects only to a numerically larger AC, or when force is set). Otherwise it reads the queue's ra_sta_id, tx fifo and tid, notes whether the queue is shared (tid_bitmap has more than one bit), sets IWL_MVM_TXQ_STATE_STOP_REDIRECT on txq and waits for the queue to drain; if the wait fails it returns -EIO via the out label (the queue is not disabled in that case). Otherwise it disables the queue (iwl_trans_txq_disable) and sends SCD_QUEUE_CFG with the disable action; that command's result is stored in ret and an error is only logged, execution continues. It then re-enables the queue config with the ssn, sets queue_info[queue].txq_tid = tid, calls iwl_mvm_reconfig_scd (return value ignored), sets mac80211_ac = ac and, if shared, sets shared mode in the transport. At out it clears STOP_REDIRECT and returns ret, which is -EIO on drain failure, else the result of the SCD disable command (0 or its error), so a failed disable command is returned even though the redirect was carried on.
note: Reviewers: original right (redirect when ac is numerically larger unless force, line 726); round 15 WRONG in this source: the enable path ignores iwl_mvm_reconfig_scd (767-769, no assignment to ret), so ret comes from the disable command at 754 and a disable failure is returned, not 0.

name: iwl_mvm_stop_roc
prose: Stops a remain-on-channel (time-event.c:1252). It locks mvm->mutex itself (1261). Branch 1: if the device has P2P over aux, or the ROC_CMD version is >= 3 and the vif is not P2P_DEVICE, then if mvmvif->roc_activity < ROC_NUM_ACTIVITIES it sends iwl_mvm_roc_rm_cmd for that activity and sets roc_activity = ROC_NUM_ACTIVITIES (only in that case), then goes to cleanup_roc. Branch 2: else, with the SESSION_PROT_CMD capability: for a P2P_DEVICE vif, if te_data->id >= SESSION_PROTECT_CONF_MAX_ID it logs, unlocks the mutex and returns without any cleanup; else it cancels the session protection; for other vif types it removes the aux ROC time event for hs_time_event_data; then cleanup_roc. Branch 3 (older firmware): te_data = iwl_mvm_get_roc_te; if NULL it warns, unlocks and returns; otherwise it switches to that te_data's vif and removes the time event (P2P_DEVICE) or the aux ROC time event (other types), then falls to cleanup_roc. At cleanup_roc it SETS (not clears) IWL_MVM_STATUS_ROC_AUX_RUNNING if p2p_aux or the vif type is not P2P_DEVICE, else IWL_MVM_STATUS_ROC_P2P_RUNNING, so that iwl_mvm_cleanup_roc does the cleanup even if the ROC had not started; it then calls iwl_mvm_cleanup_roc(mvm), which test-and-clears those bits, removes the p2p bcast/aux station as applicable and itself calls mutex_unlock(&mvm->mutex) (time-event.c:126), so on the cleanup_roc path this function does not unlock separately. Returns void; the mutex is released on every exit.
note: Reviewers: original right (roc_activity reset only in the first branch; early returns exist for P2P_DEVICE without te and for no ROC te); round 15 half right: the bits are SET at 1309-1312 (reviewer wrong), cleared by iwl_mvm_cleanup_roc; the mutex IS released inside iwl_mvm_cleanup_roc (reviewer right that the old prose misplaced it). Callees other than cleanup_roc not read.

name: iwl_trans_pcie_start_fw
prose: Starts firmware on a PCIe device (trans.c:1291). It first calls iwl_pcie_prepare_card_hw and returns -EIO if that is non-zero (1301-1304), before trans_pcie->mutex is taken. It then enables the RF-kill interrupt, acks CSR_INT, disables interrupts and synchronizes IRQs, and locks trans_pcie->mutex. With the mutex held it goes to out with: -ERFKILL if HW RF-kill is set and run_in_rfkill is false (1324); -EIO if trans_pcie->is_down (1330); or the non-zero error of iwl_pcie_nic_init. Otherwise it clears the RF-kill/cmd-blocked bits, enables only the firmware-load interrupt (iwl_enable_fw_load_int; the general host interrupts are not re-enabled here), and loads the image with iwl_pcie_load_given_ucode_8000 (device family >= 8000) or iwl_pcie_load_given_ucode, keeping its return value in ret. It then re-reads the HW RF-kill state and, if set and run_in_rfkill is false, overwrites ret with -ERFKILL, even if the load itself failed. At out it unlocks the mutex and returns ret, so the result is 0, -EIO, -ERFKILL, or a callee error from nic_init or the ucode load (callee values not read).
note: Reviewers: original right (the early -EIO happens before mutex_lock, no unlock needed; load errors are callee values); round 15 right (only the FW-load interrupt is enabled, 1358).

name: mt7603_pre_tbtt_tasklet
prose: Pre-TBTT tasklet of the mt7603 driver (beacon.c:101, void). If dev->mphy.offchannel is set it returns immediately and does nothing (110). Otherwise it flushes the CAB queue by writing MT_WF_ARB_CAB_FLUSH, runs mt76_queue_tx_cleanup on the CAB and BEACON queues, increments dev->beacon_check if the beacon queue still has queued frames and resets it to 0 otherwise, and calls mt7603_mac_stuck_beacon_recovery. Under the beacon queue lock it iterates active interfaces with mt7603_update_beacon_iter (which fetches and queues each beacon; in that helper, if either MT_DMA_FQCR0 poll times out it sets beacon_check to MT7603_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT and skips queueing, and the fetched beacon skb is then neither queued nor freed there) and kicks the queue. It then calls mt76_csa_check; if mdev->csa_complete is set it returns, with no CAB work. Otherwise it collects buffered broadcast/multicast frames from all interfaces via mt7603_add_buffered_bc, repeating while the count keeps growing and stays below 8. If none were collected it returns without queueing anything or starting CAB. Otherwise it clears the more-data flag on the last frame of each interface, queues all collected skbs on the CAB queue under its lock (mt76_tx_queue_skb, then kick), writes the per-BSS CAB counts, and writes MT_WF_ARB_CAB_START.
note: Reviewers: original right (CAB counts/start only if buffered frames exist; early returns skip CAB); round 15 is about mt7603_update_beacon_iter (beacon.c:~44-47 poll timeout path), which this function calls; the skb leak is real there but is not in the tasklet body. The tasklet itself does not take or free the beacon skb.

name: mt7615_mac_adjust_sensitivity
prose: Adjusts the CCK or OFDM energy-detect sensitivity (mac.c:1795, static, void). It selects false_cca, default threshold def_th (-98 for OFDM, -110 for CCK) and a pointer to the stored sensitivity, and gets signal = mt76_get_min_avg_rssi. If that is 0 it calls mt7615_mac_set_default_sensitivity and returns without anything else. Otherwise signal = min(signal, -72). If false_cca > 500: it returns at once if rts_err_rate > MT_FRAC(40,100); else if the sensitivity equals def_th and signal > -90 it sets the sensitivity to -90 (a jump of 8 for OFDM, 20 for CCK), else if sensitivity + 2 < signal it raises it by 2. Else if (0 < false_cca < 50) or rts_err_rate > MT_FRAC(60,100): if sensitivity - 2 >= def_th it lowers it by 2. Then in all non-returning cases, if the sensitivity is above signal it is clamped to signal (so it can drop by more than 2). If anything changed it writes the register value (sensitivity*2+512 for OFDM, sensitivity+256 for CCK) with mt7615_mac_set_sensitivity and records phy->last_cca_adj = jiffies. rts_err_rate is not range-checked; any u32 value is compared as given.
note: Reviewers: original right (jump to -90 from def_th is 8/20, line 1819-1821); round 15 right (rts_err_rate is an unrestricted u32 here; only the thresholds at 1815 and 1827 are compared). Callee bodies not read.

name: mt7915_get_et_stats
prose: Fills the ethtool statistics array for an mt7915 vif (main.c:1514, void). It takes dev->mt76.mutex, calls mt7915_mac_update_stats(phy), and writes the PHY MIB counters sequentially into data[] (tx counters, 15 aggregation-size counters from phy->mt76->aggr_stats, beamforming and AMSDU counters, rx counters, dl_* and ul_hetrig_* counters), advancing ei. It sets wi.initial_stat_idx = ei and iterates all stations with mt7915_ethtool_worker; for each station whose vif idx equals this vif's mt76.idx, mt76_ethtool_worker does sta_count++ and ADDS (+=) that station's per-mode counters into the same worker slots starting at initial_stat_idx (the slots are accumulated across stations, not appended per station; data[] is not zeroed by this function). It then unlocks the mutex. If wi.sta_count == 0 it returns (main.c:1635-1636), so in that case the page-pool statistics are not written. Otherwise it advances ei by wi.worker_stat_count, writes the page-pool stats via mt76_ethtool_page_pool_stats(&dev->mt76, &data[ei], &ei), and logs with dev_err if ei differs from MT7915_SSTATS_LEN + page_pool_ethtool_stats_get_count(). The caller's data buffer must therefore hold that many u64 entries.
note: Reviewers: original right (page-pool counts in the size); round 2 right (accumulation into existing slots, mac80211.c:2034 uses +=); round 15 WRONG: page-pool stats are skipped when sta_count == 0 (main.c:1635), not unconditional.

name: mt7925e_mac_reset
prose: Resets the mt7925 PCIe MAC (pci_mac.c:70). Sequence: mt792xe_mcu_drv_pmctrl (result ignored); frees pending TX skbs; disables host IRQs and PCIe MAC interrupts; sets MT76_RESET and MT76_MCU_RESET, wakes the MCU waiters and purges the MCU response queue; schedules all txqs; disables the tx worker and, depending on irq_map masks, the main/MCU/WA rx NAPIs and the tx NAPI; puts the TX tokens (mt7925_tx_token_put) and re-initialises the token idr; resets the WPDMA (mt792x_wpdma_reset(dev, true)); re-enables all rx NAPIs and the tx NAPI and schedules them (it does not schedule the tx worker); clears fw_assert and MT76_MCU_RESET; re-enables the host IRQ mask and MT_PCIE_MAC_INT_ENABLE. Then err = mt792xe_mcu_fw_pmctrl(dev); if that fails it returns err immediately (125-126) without reaching the out label, so MT76_RESET stays set and the tx worker stays disabled. Otherwise it runs, stopping at the first failure with err set: __mt792xe_mcu_drv_pmctrl, mt7925_run_firmware, mt7925_mcu_set_eeprom, mt7925_mac_init, __mt7925_start. At out it clears MT76_RESET and re-enables the tx worker (mt76_worker_enable), and returns err (0 on success).
note: Reviewers: original right (early return after fw_pmctrl failure skips out label); round 15 right (only NAPIs are scheduled, tx_worker is just re-enabled, line 148).

name: mt7996_mac_reset_work
prose: Work function for MCU/L1 SER recovery on mt7996 (mac.c:2520, void; the slice cut the head). If dev->recovery.restart is set it disables the MCU command watchdog interrupt, increments wa_reset_count (if the recovery state has MT_MCU_CMD_WA_WDT) or wm_reset_count, runs mt7996_mac_full_reset, enables MT_INT_MCU_CMD (disabling the rest), re-enables the watchdog mask, sets recovery.state = MT_MCU_CMD_NORMAL_STATE and recovery.restart = false, and returns. Otherwise it returns at once, doing nothing, if the recovery state does not have MT_MCU_CMD_STOP_DMA. Otherwise (L1 SER recovery): it logs a start message, stops any active WED devices, stops the mac80211 queues, sets MT76_RESET and MT76_MCU_RESET, aborts scans, wakes MCU waiters, cancels the WED RRO work, and for each phy aborts ROC, sets MT76_RESET and cancels mac_work synchronously; disables the tx worker and the rx NAPIs (skipping WED RRO queues when WED is active) and the tx NAPI. Then it locks dev->mt76.mutex and, with it held: stops the NPU hw, signals DMA_STOPPED, waits for the RESET_DONE state (result tested only for that one wait), and if that wait returns 0 resets the DMA, puts the TX tokens, re-inits the token idr, signals DMA_INIT and waits for RECOVERY_DONE; then signals RESET_DONE and waits for NORMAL_STATE (this wait result is ignored), restarts DMA, programs the RRO 3.0 emu config when applicable, restarts WED hardware paths when active, clears MT76_MCU_RESET and the per-phy MT76_RESET bits, re-enables and schedules the rx NAPIs, schedules the irq tasklet, re-enables the tx worker, re-enables and schedules the tx NAPI, wakes the queues and updates beacons. The mutex is released only after the beacon update (mac.c:2660); after unlocking it calls mt7996_npu_hw_init, requeues each phy's mac_work with MT7996_WATCHDOG_TIME and logs completion. No return value or error is produced for failures of the individual waits.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the mutex is held through the reset-bit clearing, NAPI/worker re-enable, queue wake and beacon update (2591-2660). Callee bodies not read.

name: mt7996_mac_sta_event
prose: Applies an association, authorization or disassociation event to every active link of a station (main.c:1158, static, returns int). It takes dev->mt76.mutex itself (1167; the caller must not hold it) and releases it at the unlock label on every path. For each active link (for_each_sta_active_link) it skips the link (continue) if link_conf, the vif link or the station link structure is NULL. ASSOC: calls mt7996_mcu_add_sta with CONN_STATE_CONNECT and, if that succeeds, mt7996_mcu_add_rate_ctrl, then sets MT_WCID_TX_INFO_SET in wcid.tx_info; the first failing MCU call jumps to unlock and its error is returned, so later links are not processed. AUTHORIZE: mt7996_mcu_add_sta with CONN_STATE_PORT_SECURE; an error is returned the same way. DISASSOC: tears down all TWT flows of the link, then for a non-MLO station calls mt7996_mcu_add_sta with CONN_STATE_DISCONNECT (its result is ignored), or for an MLO station on its last remaining link calls mt7996_mcu_teardown_mld_sta (result ignored), and then SETS msta_link->wcid.sta_disabled = 1 and sets wcid.sta = 0 and removes the link from the local links mask. Returns 0 unless an ASSOC or AUTHORIZE MCU call failed.
note: Reviewers: original right (the function locks the mutex itself, 1167); round 15 right (DISASSOC sets sta_disabled to 1 and clears wcid.sta, 1221-1222, it does not clear sta_disabled). Callees not read.

name: mt7996_set_radar_background
prose: Starts or stops the background radar (RDD2) detector (main.c:2112, static, returns int). Picks phy = mt7996_band_phy(dev, chandef->chan->band) when chandef is given, else dev->rdd2_phy; if phy is NULL it returns -EINVAL before taking the mutex (2124-2125). It then takes dev->mt76.mutex and, with ret preset to -EINVAL, goes to out (unlock, return ret) if mt76.region is NL80211_DFS_UNSET (returns -EINVAL), or returns -EBUSY via out if dev->rdd2_phy is set to a different phy. It computes running = rdd2_phy set and rdd2_chandef valid and its channel flagged IEEE80211_CHAN_RADAR. If chandef is NULL, or running, or chandef's channel is not a radar channel, it first calls mt7996_mcu_rdd_background_enable(phy, NULL) (error returned via out); if not running it then jumps to update_phy, otherwise it falls through. Otherwise (and in the running fall-through) it calls mt7996_mcu_rdd_background_enable(phy, chandef) (error returned via out). At update_phy it sets dev->rdd2_phy = phy when chandef is non-NULL and NULL otherwise, and copies *chandef into dev->rdd2_chandef only when chandef is non-NULL (rdd2_chandef is left unchanged when chandef is NULL). Returns the last MCU result (0 on success).
note: Reviewers: original right (chandef NULL does not clear rdd2_chandef; -EINVAL paths exist); round 15 right (the !phy early return happens before mutex_lock, 2124-2127, so the mutex is not held there).

name: mt7996_mcu_get_temperature
prose: Queries the firmware temperature (mcu.c:4058; the packet name mt7996_mcu_get_temp does not exist, the slice cut the head). It builds a local request (tag TEMPERATURE_QUERY, action GET_TEMPERATURE, band_idx = phy->mt76->band_idx) and calls mt76_mcu_send_and_get_msg with MCU_WM_UNI_CMD(THERMAL) and wait set. If that returns non-zero the function returns that error and no reply skb is held by it. Otherwise it reads res->temperature (a little-endian u32 at the packed reply layout) from skb->data without checking skb->len, frees the reply skb with dev_kfree_skb, and returns the converted u32 value through the int return type (a value above INT_MAX would read as negative).
note: Slice cut the head (real function at mcu.c:4058-4101). Old prose is consistent with the code; added the unchecked skb length and the u32-to-int conversion. mt76_mcu_send_and_get_msg not read.

name: mt76_testmode_tx_init
prose: Prepares the test-mode TX frame and rate (testmode.c:178, static, returns int). It first calls mt76_testmode_alloc_skb(phy, td->tx_mpdu_len) and returns its error if non-zero: -ENOMEM when the head skb allocation fails (td->tx_skb is left as it was), or -ENOMEM when a fragment allocation fails, in which case that function has already called mt76_testmode_free_skb, so the previous td->tx_skb is freed (not left unchanged); on success td->tx_skb is the newly built skb. If td->tx_rate_mode is above MT76_TM_TX_MODE_VHT it returns 0 with no rate setup. Otherwise max_nss = number of antennas, limited by td->tx_antenna_mask if set; rates[0] gets count 1 and idx = td->tx_rate_idx. By mode: CCK returns -EINVAL if the band is not 2 GHz or idx > 4; OFDM on a non-2 GHz band does no range check and keeps idx as requested, while on 2 GHz it returns -EINVAL if idx > 8 and otherwise adds 4 to idx; HT returns -EINVAL if idx > 8*max_nss unless idx == 32 with channel width >= 40 MHz, and sets IEEE80211_TX_RC_MCS; VHT returns -EINVAL if idx > 9 or td->tx_rate_nss > max_nss, then sets the VHT rate and RC_VHT_MCS flag. Then it sets SHORT_GI, LDPC, STBC when requested, and, for modes HT and above, the 40/80/160 MHz width flag from phy->chandef.width. Returns 0. The -EINVAL returns happen after the new skb was already stored in td->tx_skb, which is not freed on those paths.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (fragment allocation failure frees td->tx_skb, testmode.c:157); round 2 right (OFDM on non-2GHz skips the idx check, 210-211); round 15 right (OFDM on 2GHz adds 4, 216). Callee mt76_testmode_free_skb not read.

name: rtw_bf_assoc
prose: Registers the associated AP as a beamformee (bf.c:30, void). If the chip does not support the 5 GHz band it returns immediately (45-46), before taking rcu_read_lock, so no RCU lock is taken on that path. Otherwise it takes rcu_read_lock and looks up the AP station by bssid; if not found it unlocks, logs a warning and returns. It then takes pointers to the 5 GHz band's VHT capability and the station's deflink.vht_cap, and calls rcu_read_unlock BEFORE using those capability pointers (the station pointer is used after the RCU section ends). If the local device is MU-beamformee capable and the AP is MU-beamformer capable: it returns without changes if bfer_mu_cnt >= chip->bfer_mu_max_num (debug log); else it sets bfee mac_addr, role RTW_BFEE_MU, p_aid and aid (vif->cfg.aid), increments bfer_mu_cnt and calls rtw_chip_config_bfee(..., true); it does not touch su_reg_index or bfer_su_reg_maping. Else if SU beamformee/beamformer are both capable: it returns without changes if bfer_su_cnt >= bfer_su_max_num; else it sets mac_addr, role RTW_BFEE_SU, sound_dim from the AP's sounding dimensions, g_id 0 and p_aid, increments bfer_su_cnt, claims the first free bit in bfer_su_reg_maping for bfee->su_reg_index (if none is free su_reg_index is left unchanged), and calls rtw_chip_config_bfee(..., true). If neither case applies it does nothing more.
note: Reviewers: original right (MU path does not claim su_reg_index); round 15 right (no rcu_read_lock on the no-5GHz early return, bf.c:45-48). Note the RCU unlock at line 67 precedes use of vht_cap.

name: rtw_coex_set_ant_path
prose: Sets the coexistence antenna path for a phase (coex.c:1283, static, void). If force is false and coex_dm->cur_ant_pos_type already equals phase it returns doing nothing. Otherwise it stores phase in cur_ant_pos_type, then calls rtw_coex_check_rfk and logs bt_disabled; these happen before the switch, so they also happen for an unknown phase. Per phase: POWERON sets the coex control owner (true if bt_disabled, else false) and selects ctrl BBSW / pos TO_BT; it does not set the GNT_BT/GNT_WL signals. INIT sets GNT_BT low and GNT_WL high if bt_disabled, else GNT_BT high and GNT_WL low, takes the control owner, ctrl BBSW / pos TO_BT. WONLY sets GNT_BT low, GNT_WL high, owner true, BBSW / TO_WLG. WOFF only releases the control owner (false) and selects ctrl BY_BT / pos NOCARE, with no GNT changes. 2G sets both GNT to HW_PTA, owner true, ctrl BY_PTA / NOCARE. 5G sets GNT_BT HW_PTA and GNT_WL SW_HIGH, owner true, BBSW / TO_WLA. 2G_FREERUN sets GNT_BT HW_PTA, GNT_WL SW_HIGH, BBSW / TO_WLG_BT. 2G_WLBT sets both to HW_PTA, BBSW / TO_WLG_BT. An unknown phase executes WARN(1) and returns without calling the antenna switch. After a known phase, if the selected ctrl and pos types are both valid and coex_rfe->ant_switch_exist, it calls rtw_coex_set_ant_switch(rtwdev, ctrl_type, pos_type).
note: Reviewers: original right (POWERON and WOFF set only the control owner, no GNT writes); round 15 right (for an unknown phase cur_ant_pos_type is updated and rtw_coex_check_rfk runs before the WARN, 1295-1298 vs 1427).

name: rtw8821c_phy_pwrtrack
prose: Periodic thermal power tracking for the RTL8821C (rtw8821c.c:1092, static, void). It first calls rtw_phy_config_swing_table to fill a local swing table, and only then returns if efuse.thermal_meter[0] == 0xff (1100-1101), so the swing-table call is made even in that early-return case and no thermal read, tracking or IQK check follows. Otherwise it reads the path-A thermal meter, feeds it to rtw_phy_pwrtrack_avg, and then: if dm_info->pwr_trk_init_trigger is set it clears that flag and continues to the power computation even if the thermal value has not changed; else if rtw_phy_pwrtrack_thermal_changed reports no change it skips straight to the IQK check. The power computation gets delta (capped to RTW_PWR_TRK_TBL_SZ - 1) and the new delta_power_index[A] from the swing table; if that equals delta_power_index_last[A] it skips to the IQK check, else it stores it into delta_power_index_last and calls rtw8821c_pwrtrack_set. At the iqk label, if rtw_phy_pwrtrack_need_iqk is true it calls rtw8821c_do_iqk.
note: Reviewers: original right (the pwr_trk_init_trigger path reprograms without a thermal change); round 15 right (rtw_phy_config_swing_table runs before the 0xff return, 1098-1101). Callees not read.

name: rtw89_mcc_duration_decision_on_bt
prose: Decides how MCC role durations are adapted to the BT duration (chan.c:1691, static, returns bool). Returns false at once, changing nothing, if mcc->bt_role.duration is 0. If both the reference and auxiliary roles are on 2 GHz it calls rtw89_mcc_mod_duration_dual_2ghz_with_bt (which clamps bt_role.duration and rewrites both role durations) and returns true; this is the only path that returns true. If neither role is on 2 GHz it logs and returns false without changes. If exactly one role is on 2 GHz it calls rtw89_mcc_mod_duration_diff_band_with_bt with the 2 GHz role first and the other second, then returns false. That helper itself returns without changing anything when the non-2 GHz role's duration is already >= the BT duration (chan.c:1665-1668); otherwise it sets the non-2 GHz duration to the BT duration (capped by that role's limit.max_dur if its limit is enabled) and the 2 GHz duration to mcc_interval minus that. So in the exactly-one-2GHz case the durations may or may not be modified, and the result is false either way.
note: Reviewers: original right (false returned with no adjustment when neither role is 2GHz or bt duration is zero); round 15 right (one-2GHz case may leave durations unchanged, chan.c:1665-1668).

name: rtw89_mcc_fill_role_limit
prose: Fills the MCC time-of-arrival/-of-beacon limit of a P2P GC role from its NoA descriptor (chan.c:881, static, void). It returns immediately if !mcc_role->is_gc (894-895), before any RCU lock is taken. Otherwise it recalculates the once-NoA (rtw89_p2p_noa_once_recalc), takes rcu_read_lock, dereferences the link's bss_conf and scans its P2P NoA descriptors for one with count == 255; if none is found it calls rcu_read_unlock and returns (910-911). If found, it copies start_time, interval and duration and unlocks RCU. It then returns without enabling a limit if the NoA interval differs from the beacon interval in us, if rtw89_mac_port_get_tsf fails (warning), if max_toa_us or max_tob_us is 0 (boundary), or if max_dur_us < max_toa_us. Otherwise it sets limit.max_toa, max_tob (both microseconds divided by 1024), limit.max_dur = max_toa + max_tob and limit.enable = true. The early returns do not write limit.enable or any other limit field; whatever value the role already had is kept, which relies on the caller having cleared the role beforehand.
note: Reviewers: original right (it does not clear limit.enable on early returns, relies on caller zeroing); round 15 right (no RCU lock on the !is_gc early return, 894-899). The caller's zeroing was not checked.

name: _chk_btc_err
prose: Updates a BTC error counter/flag selected by type (coex.c:1103, static, void). It logs type and cnt, then switches on type; an unlisted type changes nothing. WL_FW_VER_MATCH sets wl->fw_ver_mismatch and error.map.wl_ver_mismatch to whether the high 16 bits of wl->ver_info.fw_coex differ from chip->wlcx_desired (cnt is unused). The hang types RPT, CYCLE, W1, B1 and E2G each compare the passed cnt with the value stored last time in cnt_dm[...]; if equal AND their extra condition holds (RPT: btc->fwinfo.rpt_en_map non-zero; CYCLE: tdma_now.type != CXTDMA_OFF or ext_ctrl == CXECTL_EXT; W1 and B1: tdma_now.type != CXTDMA_OFF; E2G: ext_ctrl == CXECTL_EXT) the matching *_HANG counter is incremented, else reset to 0; the corresponding error.map flag is set when that counter >= BTC_CHK_HANG_MAX and cleared otherwise, and the stored cnt_dm value is updated to cnt. TDMA_NONSYNC and SLOT_NONSYNC increment their counter when cnt != 0, else reset it, and set tdma_no_sync/slot_no_sync when the counter >= BTC_CHK_HANG_MAX (no stored cnt update). BTTX_HANG ignores the passed cnt and uses cx->cnt_bt[BTC_BCNT_LOPRI_TX]: it counts up if that is 0 and bt->link_info.slave_role is set, else resets, and sets error.map.bt_tx_hang at the maximum. BTCNT_HANG likewise ignores cnt and sums the four BT hi/lo-pri rx/tx counters: counts up while the sum is 0, else resets; and calls _update_bt_scbd(rtwdev, false) when the counter has reached the maximum while bt->enable.now is set, or when the counter is 0 while bt->enable.now is clear. WL_SLOT_DRIFT and BT_SLOT_DRIFT count up when cnt >= BTC_CHK_WLSLOT_DRIFT_MAX / BTC_CHK_BTSLOT_DRIFT_MAX, else reset, and set wl_slot_drift/bt_slot_drift at the maximum.
note: Reviewers: original right (WL_FW_VER_MATCH and BTCNT_HANG do not follow the counter/max pattern; BTTX_HANG ignores cnt, 1219); round 15 right (CYCLE_HANG condition is type != OFF OR ext_ctrl == EXT, 1141-1142).

name: rtw89_debugfs_file_read
prose: Generic debugfs read for rtw89 (debug.c:155, static). bufsz is opt->rsize or PAGE_SIZE. If debugfs_priv->rbuf is NULL it allocates it with devm_kzalloc(bufsz); if the buffer is still NULL it returns -ENOMEM. If *ppos is non-zero it uses n = debugfs_priv->rused (the byte count saved by the previous read at position 0) and returns simple_read_from_buffer(userbuf, count, ppos, buf, n), whose result depends on ppos and count and is not itself the cached count. If *ppos is 0 and opt->rlock is set, it calls wiphy_locked_debugfs_read(... rtw89_debugfs_file_read_helper ...), stores its result in rused and returns it directly (that helper copies to userbuf itself). If *ppos is 0 and rlock is clear it calls rtw89_debugfs_file_read_helper(wiphy, file, buf, bufsz, debugfs_priv) with no lock taken by this function, stores the result in rused (a negative result is stored as-is, converted to the rused type) and returns simple_read_from_buffer(userbuf, count, ppos, buf, n) with that n. The helper's callback behaviour was not read, so what a non-positive callback result does is not claimed here.
note: Reviewers: original right (non-zero ppos returns the simple_read_from_buffer result); round 2 partly checked (negative n is passed on to simple_read_from_buffer unchanged, line 187-192, no clamping here); round 15 right (cb_read runs under wiphy lock when opt->rlock is set, 177-184). Helper not read.

name: rtw89_debug_mac_dump_dle_dbg
prose: Formats the DLE (WDE/PLE) debug registers into buf (debug.c:1253, static, returns int; the slice cut the head). It first calls rtw89_mac_check_mac_en(rtwdev, 0, RTW89_DMAC_SEL); if that fails it writes '[DLE]  : DMAC not enabled' into buf and returns the bytes written (a non-negative length via the out label). Otherwise it dumps free-page head/tail and public page count for WDE and PLE and then, for each quota id of WDE (up to WDE_QTAID_CPUIO) and of PLE (up to PLE_QTAID_CPUIO), rsv_pgnum and use_pgnum, appending text with scnprintf. Each register read goes through the local macro DLE_DFI_DUMP, which writes the DFI control register and polls it with read_poll_timeout (1000 us interval, 50000 us limit); on timeout the macro logs an error and executes return __ret, so this function then returns the (negative) poll error immediately, with the text appended so far left in buf. If all reads succeed it returns p - buf, the number of bytes written.
note: Slice cut the head (real function at debug.c:1253). Reviewer round 15 WRONG: the DLE_DFI_DUMP macro contains 'return __ret;' on a poll timeout (debug.c:1273-1277), so the timeout is not ignored in this function; its callee-level poll error code was not read (value from read_poll_timeout).
